strings.d1.s0.name: Sagrada Família
strings.d1.s0.tips: Gaudí's basilica. Book timed tickets online weeks ahead (centenary year 2026, 26-40 EUR); the tower costs extra. At 09:00 the light hits the stained glass.
strings.d1.s1.name: Casa Batlló
strings.d1.s1.tips: The house with the dragon-back roof. Book online, morning slot.
strings.d1.s2.name: Casa Milà La Pedrera
strings.d1.s2.tips: Admire the wavy façade from outside; the interior is an optional 28 EUR.
strings.d1.s3.name: Cerveseria Catalana
strings.d1.s3.tips: Classic Eixample tapas bar. Try the montaditos (small open sandwiches) and gambas (prawns); the queue is short at 13:30.
strings.d1.s4.name: Passeig de Gràcia
strings.d1.b0.name: Tapas 24
strings.d1.b0.tips: Carles Abellan's tapas bar; try the bikini sandwich.
strings.d1.b1.name: Recinte Modernista Sant Pau
strings.d1.b1.tips: Modernist hospital complex near the Sagrada Família; a calmer alternative to Batlló.
strings.d2.s0.name: Barcelona Cathedral
strings.d2.s0.tips: Gothic cathedral with a cloister courtyard of geese. Free mass hours in the morning.
strings.d2.s1.name: Barri Gòtic Streets
strings.d2.s1.tips: Plaça Sant Felip Neri, the Roman columns (MUHBA Temple d'August, free) and the Bisbe bridge.
strings.d2.s2.name: La Boqueria
strings.d2.s2.tips: Market on the Rambla. Eat squid with eggs at the El Quim or Bar Pinotxo counter; best before 10:00.
strings.d2.s3.name: Santa Maria del Mar
strings.d2.s3.tips: The Cathedral of the Sea; plain, pure Gothic.
strings.d2.s4.name: Picasso Museum
strings.d2.s4.tips: Early-period Picasso. Free on Thursday evenings, book online.
strings.d2.b0.name: El Xampanyet
strings.d2.b0.tips: Serving cava and anchovies since 1929; standing room, next to the Picasso Museum.
strings.d2.b1.name: Palau de la Música Catalana
strings.d2.b1.tips: Tour of the Modernist concert hall; an alternative to the Picasso Museum.
strings.d3.s0.name: Park Güell
strings.d3.s0.tips: Mosaic salamander and the wavy bench. Timed online tickets (10 EUR); the 08:30 first slot is quiet.
strings.d3.s1.name: Bunkers del Carmel
strings.d3.s1.tips: Former anti-aircraft hill; Barcelona's best free 360° view.
strings.d3.s2.name: Plaça del Sol, Gràcia
strings.d3.s2.tips: Village-feel neighbourhood with squares and terraces.
strings.d3.s3.name: La Pubilla
strings.d3.s3.tips: Catalan set lunch in Gràcia; closed on Sundays.
strings.d3.s4.name: Casa Vicens
strings.d3.s4.tips: Gaudí's first house in Gràcia, with tile and palm-leaf motifs.
strings.d3.b0.name: Bar Bodega Quimet Gràcia
strings.d3.b0.tips: Vermouth and tinned-seafood tapas; a local spot.
strings.d3.b1.name: Hospital de Sant Pau
strings.d3.b1.tips: Modernist hospital; an alternative to Casa Vicens.
strings.d4.s0.name: MNAC Museu Nacional
strings.d4.s0.tips: Romanesque frescoes in a palace building. Enjoy the city view from the steps; the terrace is free.
strings.d4.s1.name: Fundació Joan Miró
strings.d4.s1.tips: Works by Miró in Sert's white building.
strings.d4.s2.name: Montjuïc Cable Car
strings.d4.s2.tips: Cable car up to the castle, with sea views.
strings.d4.s3.name: Montjuïc Castle Café
strings.d4.s3.tips: Lunch in the castle courtyard with a view of the harbour.
strings.d4.s4.name: Poble Espanyol
strings.d4.s4.tips: A replica town of Spanish villages with craft workshops; the fountain is switched off.
strings.d4.b0.name: Quimet & Quimet
strings.d4.b0.tips: Legendary tinned-seafood tapas bar in Poble Sec; standing only.
strings.d4.b1.name: Montjuïc Olympic Stadium
strings.d4.b1.tips: The 1992 stadium; an alternative to the cable car.
strings.d5.s0.name: Barceloneta Beach
strings.d5.s0.tips: Winter beach walk and cycling, with surfers on the water.
strings.d5.s1.name: La Cova Fumada
strings.d5.s1.tips: Birthplace of the bomba (potato croquette). No menu, cash only, full by 13:00.
strings.d5.s2.name: Barceloneta Seafront to W Hotel
strings.d5.s2.tips: Palm-lined seafront walk, ending at Frank Gehry's fish sculpture.
strings.d5.s3.name: Port Vell and Maremagnum
strings.d5.s3.tips: The old harbour and the Rambla de Mar bridge.
strings.d5.s4.name: Transbordador Aeri del Port
strings.d5.s4.tips: Red cable car across the harbour to Montjuïc, with sea and city views.
strings.d5.b0.name: Can Paixano
strings.d5.b0.tips: Cava and sandwiches; standing only, cheap.
strings.d5.b1.name: Museu d'Història de Catalunya
strings.d5.b1.tips: History museum in a harbour warehouse, with a terrace café.
strings.d6.s0.name: Montserrat Monastery
strings.d6.s0.tips: Train plus rack railway takes 1.5 hours (about 50 EUR combined ticket). The Black Madonna sits in the saw-toothed mountain; the boys' choir (Escolania) sings at 13:00.
strings.d6.s1.name: Sant Joan Funicular
strings.d6.s1.tips: Funicular to the summit, with walking trails.
strings.d6.s2.name: Sant Joan Walk, Montserrat
strings.d6.s2.tips: A flat 1-hour walk among the rocks with views over Catalonia.
strings.d6.s3.name: Restaurant Abat Cisneros
strings.d6.s3.tips: Restaurant of the monastery hotel; Catalan lunch.
strings.d6.s4.name: Montserrat Market Stalls
strings.d6.s4.tips: Mató (fresh goat's cheese) and honey from farmers' stalls.
strings.d6.b0.name: Montserrat Self-Service Cafeteria
strings.d6.b1.name: Santa Cova
strings.d6.b1.tips: Path to the cave where the Virgin was found; an alternative to Sant Joan.
strings.d7.theme: Rambla morning and a gentle goodbye
strings.d7.s0.name: La Rambla
strings.d7.s0.tips: Walk the Rambla before the crowds arrive, past the Miró mosaic and the flower stalls.
strings.d7.s1.name: Palau Güell
strings.d7.s1.tips: Gaudí's city palace, with rooftop chimneys.
strings.d7.s2.name: Granja Viader
strings.d7.s2.tips: Hot chocolate and churros since 1870; the dairy where Cacaolat was born.
strings.d7.s3.name: Plaça Reial
strings.d7.s3.tips: Palm-filled square with Gaudí lamp posts. Take a farewell photo, then catch the Aerobús at Plaça Catalunya.
strings.d7.b0.name: Bar Lobo
strings.d7.b1.name: MACBA
strings.d7.b1.tips: Contemporary art and skateboarders; an alternative to Palau Güell.
strings.note0: Get a T-casual 10-ride metro ticket; the Aerobús from Plaça Catalunya takes 35 minutes. The city is walkable, and Montjuïc has a cable car and funicular.
strings.note1: Sagrada Família, Park Güell, Casa Batlló, Picasso: timed online tickets are ESSENTIAL. For the Sagrada Família, book months ahead because of the 2026 centenary.
strings.note2: Winter is sunny at 10-15°C with no crowds. December brings the Christmas market (Fira de Santa Llúcia), January the sales; the Font Màgica is limited in winter.
strings.note3: The set lunch (menú del día) costs 13-18 EUR, about half the price of dinner. Standing at tapas bars is cheap. Dinner starts after 21:00.
strings.note4: Pickpocketing on the Rambla and the metro is among the worst in Europe: keep your bag in front and never leave your phone on the table.
strings.note5: Catalan and Spanish are spoken; 'bon dia' is enough. For a tip, round up the bill.
